python3 -c "
import math

# National Defense expenditures from Table 4 (in millions of dollars)
exp = {
    1933: 680,
    1934: 531,
    1935: 689,
    1936: 900,
    1937: 929,
    1938: 1029,
    1939: 1206,
    1940: 1657,
    1941: 6301
}

years = sorted(exp.keys())
print('National Defense Expenditures (millions of dollars):')
for y in years:
    print(f'  FY{y}: {exp[y]}')

# Year-to-year log growth rates: ln(Y_t / Y_{t-1})
log_growth = []
for i in range(1, len(years)):
    y_curr = years[i]
    y_prev = years[i-1]
    lg = math.log(exp[y_curr] / exp[y_prev])
    log_growth.append((y_curr, lg))
    print(f'  Log growth FY{y_prev}->FY{y_curr}: {lg:.6f}')

# Coefficient of variation = population stdev / mean
n = len(log_growth)
mean_lg = sum(log_growth[i][1] for i in range(n)) / n
print(f'\nMean log growth rate: {mean_lg:.6f}')

# Population standard deviation
variance = sum((log_growth[i][1] - mean_lg)**2 for i in range(n)) / n
pstdev = math.sqrt(variance)
print(f'Population std dev: {pstdev:.6f}')

cv = pstdev / abs(mean_lg)
print(f'\nCV = {pstdev:.6f} / {abs(mean_lg):.6f} = {cv:.6f}')
print(f'CV rounded to nearest hundredth: {round(cv, 2)}')
"

python3 -c "
import math

# National Defense expenditures from Table 4 (in millions of dollars)
exp = {
    1933: 680,
    1934: 531,
    1935: 689,
    1936: 900,
    1937: 929,
    1938: 1029,
    1939: 1206,
    1940: 1657,
    1941: 6301
}

# Year-to-year log growth rates
years = sorted(exp.keys())
log_growth_rates = []
for i in range(1, len(years)):
    lg = math.log(exp[years[i]] / exp[years[i-1]])
    log_growth_rates.append(lg)

print('Log growth rates:', [round(x,6) for x in log_growth_rates])
print('N =', len(log_growth_rates))

# Mean
mean_lg = sum(log_growth_rates) / len(log_growth_rates)
print('Mean:', mean_lg)

# Population std dev (divide by N, not N-1)
variance = sum((x - mean_lg)**2 for x in log_growth_rates) / len(log_growth_rates)
pstdev = math.sqrt(variance)
print('Population stdev:', pstdev)

# CV
cv = pstdev / abs(mean_lg)
print('CV:', cv)
print('CV to nearest hundredth:', round(cv, 2))
"
